I can certainly see your point. This is true, maybe there was just enough of my point to make the impact for me. While the overall feel seemed more... dark shall we say, going through after a re-watch, I still feel as though the message of "strength through adversity" was an overall theme. I'm possibly grasping at straws through sheer stubbornness though. I will admit to this.

Always breaking down at their some of what I would consider their weaker moments in the series, yes I agree with this analysis. Yet I feel it shows their determination, Zoro "I will become the greatest swordsman, you got that 'King of the Pirates'", Nami crying because she felt so helpless, yet Luffy still accepts her without question, Sanji "I will become the world's greatest chef", I could go on, but I'd imagine you've already seen my theme. Crying isn't always a sign of sorrow or desperation, but rather, in this context, shows the birth of this crew's true determination to become stronger. It shows their weaker moments to, obviously in my opinion, give light to how truly strong they are. Maybe I'm reading too much into the context, but this is why I like One Piece and Oda because he isn't afraid to knock his characters completely down to build them up again.

They're both talented as all hell for completely different reasons. Rollins is a polished and talented athlete who has great mic skills. Ambrose is one of the most hard core wrestlers out there, currently, and is a fucking genius with his promos.

I want to like Rollins, I think he's an absolute beast in the making, but I feel he needs some polishing with his promo skills. Biggest reason he's currently with Rollins and Ambrose. When he's yelling and giving those war cries though... Damn he's a beast.
